2. Before every move, check hanging pieces and opponent threats, including checks and mating nets.
3. When ahead, keep it simple; when a mating attack is available, calculate it fully.
4. Keep king safe; trade attacking pieces when defending.
5. Read the board view carefully each turn; never make an illegal or careless move.
6. Accept draws in dead-equal positions only when the score favours caution.
7. Game cap: 40 moves each, then scored on material. Count moves from the start. If I am ahead in material, convert before the cap; if behind, activate pieces and grab pawns early, because material decides the score.
8. Endgames: a passive king gets nothing. Win loose pawns quickly and avoid slow manoeuvres that waste the move budget.
9. Game 2 (Black): drew at the cap, a pawn down, after an aimless king walk (Kb4 vs a2). Start the plan earlier and calculate whether it wins material in time.
10. Game 1 record: won as White by checkmate in 31 moves. Game 2 record: drawn as Black at the cap.
